index.title: Retention and holds
index.description: How long records are kept, and what is on hold because a claim is in play.
index.policyLine: Operational records stay active for {months} months. Financial records are kept for {financial} years. Archived records are purged {purge} years later.
index.policyNote: The periods are changed in Settings, and changing them has legal consequences. This system applies the numbers it is given; it does not decide which ones are right for your company.
index.purgeOn: Permanent purge is ON on this server
index.purgeOnHint: Sunday's sweep really deletes what appears below. It cannot be undone.
index.purgeOffHint: The sweep archives — which can be undone — and deletes nothing. The list below is a forecast, not what will happen.

holds.title: Active holds
holds.empty: There is no legal hold in force.
holds.reasonHint: Write it for whoever reads it in three years and has to decide whether it can be lifted. A hold with no reason never gets lifted.
holds.releaseHint: Lifting restarts the deletion clock on these records. Explain why.

purge.title: What would be purged today
purge.empty: There is nothing to purge today.
purge.hint: Expired and already archived. Anything a hold covers is left alone.

runs.title: Recent runs
runs.empty: The retention sweep has not run yet.
runs.emptyHint: It runs Sundays at 4:00 if the scheduler is enabled on the server. You can check that in Platform health.
runs.ranWithNothingToDo: The sweep ran on {date} and there was nothing to archive or purge. That is normal while the company is young.

errors.needsEntityType: A hold by type or by record needs to know which type.
errors.needsEntityId: A hold on one record needs to know which one.
errors.holdNotFound: That hold does not exist or has already been lifted.
